name: obligations-list-is-names-not-distances
description: An "N open obligations" list is N names, not N distances — check each pair for implication, because the arrow runs opposite to how the assembly was written

A headline listing N open obligations says nothing about their independence, and
readers add them. Measured 2026-07-29 (AJC, run 0084 r2): of the Jacobian headline's
five, obligation 4 (relative dimension of `Pic0SchemeEt`) **implies** obligation 2
(geometric reducedness of the same object). Both `ajc-p3` and I found it the same hour,
and a fresh-context audit confirmed it.

**Why:** the file's assembly runs 2 ⇒ 4 (reducedness → smoothness → +number → relative
dimension), and that is the direction every docstring narrates. The reverse arrow is not
in any proof — it lives in the **class hierarchy**
(`SmoothOfRelativeDimension.smooth` then `Smooth.geometricallyReduced`). A stronger
conclusion carries its own weaker inputs back out, and the assembly's prose is the last
place that will say so. It also needed the composite bridge to be outside the cone of
the file owning the weaker obligation, so a local synthesis probe read as absence
([[failing-inferinstance-is-not-absence]], measure at the root).

**How to apply:** before pricing a round off an obligations list, run n(n−1) `exact?` /
instance probes asking whether A's *conclusion* implies B's, at the **root** import.
Seconds each. Report it as a **count** correction, not a strategy one: 4 ⇒ 2 does not
make 2 cheaper — 2 is the weaker statement, the implication is useless for proving it,
and the right attack on 2 is unchanged.

**The trap next door, which I fell into the same session.** Having found a real
implication, I went on to claim the *stronger* obligation was also *one* obligation
rather than two, because unfolding its class gave a hypothesis with no smoothness in
it. That was false and the audit refuted it — see
[[unfolded-class-is-not-a-reduction]]. Finding one true structural fact about a list is
not licence for the next structural claim; each needs its own probe.
See also [[gap-count-vs-gap-cost]], [[reprice-the-prescription-before-paying-it]].

---
name: unfolded-class-is-not-a-reduction
description: An iff from HasRingHomProperty is the class definition unfolded — .mpr of it reduces nothing, and its forall-form is harder than the class it replaces
metadata:
  type: feedback
---

Unfolding a typeclass into chart language feels like a reduction and is not. Measured
2026-07-29 (AJC run 0084 r2, my own claim, refuted by a `work-reviewer` audit; I
reproduced the refutation before accepting).

The leaf was `SmoothOfRelativeDimension n f`. `HasRingHomProperty.iff_appLE` turns it
into a condition on affine chart pairs. I stated `.mpr` of that as a reduction with **no
smoothness hypothesis** and concluded "the leaf is one obligation, the smoothness half is
absorbed". Two defects:

- the hypothesis has no smoothness in it because `iff_appLE`'s right-hand side **is** the
  class. Nothing was absorbed. The absorption lemma I cited as the mechanism
  (`IsStandardSmoothOfRelativeDimension.isStandardSmooth`) was invoked by **no
  declaration in my own file** — `#print` on the theorem showed the body was exactly
  `(iff … ).mpr h`.
- the unfolded form was **harder** than the class. `SmoothOfRelativeDimension`'s field is
  *pointwise-existential* (`∀ x, ∃ U V affine, …`): one chart pair per point. The `iff`'s
  RHS demands the condition at *every* pair. So I pointed the next prover at more work
  than mathlib asks.

**How to apply:** before calling any `iff`-derived statement a reduction, `#print` the
theorem and read its body — if it is `.mpr` of an unfolding, say so in the docstring.
Then `#print` the **class** and compare quantifiers: if the class field is
`∀ x, ∃ …` and your hypothesis is `∀ …`, you have strengthened, not reduced. The honest
target is usually the anonymous constructor over the pointwise form.

Corollary I also got wrong in the same file: a failing `inferInstance` for a
`HasRingHomProperty` is not a mathematical absence — the proposition may be a library
`iff` ([[failing-inferinstance-is-not-absence]]). And an equality proved by one `rw` that
holds for an *arbitrary* property carries no content about the property you care about;
check genericity before drawing a conclusion from it, or you will dismiss a live route
(I dismissed homogeneity, which the pointwise field makes exactly the right route).
See also [[obligations-list-is-names-not-distances]].
